sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Seattle is a city with plenty of well-known tourist attractions.
sentences.zh: 西雅图是一座拥有众多知名旅游景点的城市。

sentences.en: The Space Needle, Pike Place Market, the Seattle Art Museum.
sentences.zh: 太空针塔、派克市场、西雅图艺术博物馆。

sentences.en: Today, though, I'm venturing out in the rain to visit a different sort of Seattle attraction.
sentences.zh: 不过今天，我要冒雨去参观一种不同类型的西雅图景点。

sentences.en: It's an office building called the Bullet Center.
sentences.zh: 这是一栋名为“布利特中心”的办公楼。

sentences.en: I'm here to meet Brian Court, one of the architects.
sentences.zh: 我来这里是为了见布赖恩·库尔特，他是建筑师之一。

sentences.en: Hey, Brian, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 嘿，布赖恩，我是尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Shankar, nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: Very nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 非常高兴认识你。

sentences.en: Thank you for doing this at short notice.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你能在百忙之中抽出时间。

sentences.en: Brian and I are headed to the top floor.
sentences.zh: 布赖恩和我正前往顶楼。

sentences.en: My first instinct is to find the elevator.
sentences.zh: 我的第一直觉是找电梯。

sentences.en: But it's nowhere in sight.
sentences.zh: 但电梯根本不见踪影。

sentences.en: Did you forget to put an elevator in the building, Brian?
sentences.zh: 布赖恩，你是不是忘了在楼里装电梯了？

sentences.en: We do have an elevator through the door to the left.
sentences.zh: 左边门过去确实有一部电梯。

sentences.en: If you're in a wheelchair or you're not able to climb the stairs,
sentences.zh: 如果你坐轮椅或者爬不了楼梯，

sentences.en: you just hit the button there with the wheelchair and that door will open.
sentences.zh: 只要按一下轮椅标志的按钮，那扇门就会打开。

sentences.en: But we were trying to give people an option to take the stair firSt.
sentences.zh: 但我们试图给人们提供一个首先走楼梯的选项。

sentences.en: Those stairs?
sentences.zh: 那些楼梯？

sentences.en: There are six floors of Douglas First Steps built on an outer wall of the building.
sentences.zh: 大楼的外墙上建有六层道格拉斯台阶。

sentences.en: Each floor has expansive landings that allow people to congregate and chat.
sentences.zh: 每层都有宽敞的平台，供人们聚集和聊天。

sentences.en: The best views at the Bullet Center are not from the CEO's office.
sentences.zh: 在布利特中心，最佳视野不在首席执行官办公室。

sentences.en: You get those views when you climb what people here refer to as the irresistible staircase.
sentences.zh: 当你爬上这里人们所说的“诱人楼梯”时，就能欣赏到那样的美景。

sentences.en: So you walk into the stair enclosure.
sentences.zh: 所以你走进步梯间。

sentences.en: You look up.
sentences.zh: 你抬头向上看。

sentences.en: You see the stair all the way up to the sixth floor of the building.
sentences.zh: 你能看到一直通往大楼六楼的楼梯。

sentences.en: And that's hopefully going to draw you up the stair.
sentences.zh: 希望这能吸引你顺着楼梯走上去。

sentences.en: The designers wanted to build a staircase that would help people become healthier.
sentences.zh: 设计师们希望建造一座能帮助人们变得更健康的楼梯。

sentences.en: Their intuition was that if the stairs were appealing and prominent, people would use them.
sentences.zh: 他们的直觉是，如果楼梯既吸引人又显眼，人们就会使用它们。

sentences.en: What you see as you climb to the sixth floor are sweeping views of Seattle.
sentences.zh: 当你爬到六楼时，映入眼帘的是西雅图的广阔全景。

sentences.en: You'll notice as we get higher, the views of the city really start to unfold.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，随着我们越爬越高，城市的景色真正开始展现在眼前。

sentences.en: This corner of the project site had some of the best views you can see out now to the west
sentences.zh: 项目基地的这个角落拥有一些最佳视野，现在你可以向西望去，

sentences.en: and then the downtown skyline directly to the south.
sentences.zh: 正南方则是市中心的天际线。

sentences.en: By putting a stair here, we were able to really capitalize on views
sentences.zh: 通过在这里设置楼梯，我们得以真正充分利用

sentences.en: all the way from the east around to the weSt.
sentences.zh: 从东面一直延伸到西面的美景。

sentences.en: So far, Brian says, this irresistible staircase seems to be living up to its name.
sentences.zh: 布赖恩说，到目前为止，这座诱人的楼梯似乎名不虚传。

sentences.en: We've actually got data that's showing us that just about two-thirds of the people
sentences.zh: 我们实际拥有的数据显示，

sentences.en: that go to the sixth floor on a daily basis are taking the stair over the elevator.
sentences.zh: 每天去六楼的人中，大约有三分之二选择走楼梯而不是乘电梯。

sentences.en: Most buildings place the elevators front and center as you walk inside.
sentences.zh: 大多数建筑把电梯放在一进门的正中央。

sentences.en: Most of us don't even think to look for the stairs when we enter an office building.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人在进办公楼时甚至都不会想到去找楼梯。

sentences.en: By making the stairs prominent and keeping the elevators out of sight,
sentences.zh: 通过让楼梯显眼并将电梯隐蔽起来，

sentences.en: the bullet center is trying to get people to develop new behaviors.
sentences.zh: 布利特中心正试图让人们养成新的行为习惯。

sentences.en: Sometimes, unexpected things happen as you climb these stairs.
sentences.zh: 有时，当你爬这些楼梯时，会发生意想不到的事情。

sentences.en: You bump into people you didn't think you'd meet.
sentences.zh: 你会偶遇那些你以为不会遇到的人。

sentences.en: When I was passing, I heard you talk about me walking up the stairs.
sentences.zh: 我路过的时候，听到你们在讨论我走楼梯的事。

sentences.en: I was like, that sounded like, is that?
sentences.zh: 当时我想，听起来像是，难道是……？

sentences.en: So, I just wanted to come down and say hello.
sentences.zh: 所以，我只是想下来打个招呼。

sentences.en: That's Rashad Morris.
sentences.zh: 那是拉沙德·莫里斯。

sentences.en: He walked down a flight of stairs to come say hello.
sentences.zh: 他走下一段楼梯来打招呼。

sentences.en: He told me he takes the stairs nearly every day.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他几乎每天都走楼梯。

sentences.en: And he often has chance interactions on them that turn out to be very enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 而且他在楼梯上经常有意外的偶遇，结果都非常愉快。

sentences.en: Do you actually think about it each day, that you're saying, I want to take the stairs,
sentences.zh: 你每天真的会去想这件事，告诉自己“我想走楼梯”，

sentences.en: or is it just sort of an unconscious decision at this point?
sentences.zh: 还是说到了这个时候这只是一种无意识的决定？

sentences.en: There are some times when I'm coming from downtown and I've walked all the way up Capitol Hill
sentences.zh: 有时我从市中心过来，一路走上国会山，

sentences.en: and I get to the door of the building and I think, oh man, another six flights?
sentences.zh: 走到大楼门口时，我想，天哪，还要爬六层楼？

sentences.en: But then I think, you know, I don't get a whole lot of exercise in my day-to-day work life anyway,
sentences.zh: 但转念一想，你知道的，我日常工作生活中本来就没有太多锻炼，

sentences.en: and so this is worth it, and I enjoy the view always.
sentences.zh: 所以这是值得的，而且我总是很享受这里的风景。

sentences.en: There's a word for such behaviors.
sentences.zh: 这类行为有一个专属名词。

sentences.en: They're habits.
sentences.zh: 它们是习惯。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we consider how habits shape who we are
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》节目中，我们探讨习惯如何塑造了我们，

sentences.en: and how we can use them to become the people we'd like to be.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何利用习惯成为我们想成为的人。

sentences.en: You probably know someone like this in your life.
sentences.zh: 你生活中可能也认识这样的人。

sentences.en: The person who gets a ton of things done, eats healthy food, and stays in shape.
sentences.zh: 那种能完成大量工作、饮食健康且保持身材的人。

sentences.en: People like Chris Traeger from the TV series Parks and Recreation.
sentences.zh: 就像电视剧《公园与游憩》里的克里斯·特雷格那样的人。

sentences.en: Sorry, Leslie.
sentences.zh: 对不起，莱斯利。

sentences.en: Damn!
sentences.zh: 见鬼！

sentences.en: I have to go run 10 miles.
sentences.zh: 我得去跑 10 英里。

sentences.en: I have run 10 miles a day, every day, for 18 years.
sentences.zh: 我每天都跑 10 英里，连续 18 年，天天如此。

sentences.en: That's 65,000 miles.
sentences.zh: 那是 6.5 万英里。

sentences.en: A third of the way to the moon.
sentences.zh: 到月球三分之一的距离。

sentences.en: My goal is to run to the moon.
sentences.zh: 我的目标是跑向月球。

sentences.en: Picture a guy who strips off his work clothes to reveal a running outfit underneath.
sentences.zh: 想象一下这样一个家伙，他脱掉工作服，露出里面穿的跑步装备。

sentences.en: Now, Chris Traeger is a fictional character, exaggerated for comedic effect.
sentences.zh: 当然，克里斯·特雷格是一个虚构人物，为了喜剧效果进行了夸张。

sentences.en: But we all know someone like this, a friend or colleague or spouse,
sentences.zh: 但我们都认识这样的人，一个朋友、同事或配偶，

sentences.en: who consistently performs the tasks that seem so hard to the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 他们始终如一地执行着对我们其他人来说难如登天的任务。

sentences.en: How do they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: What do they have that the rest of us lack?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么是我们其他人所缺乏的？

sentences.en: According to Wendy Wood, a professor of psychology and business at the University of Southern California,
sentences.zh: 根据南加州大学心理学和商业教授温迪·伍德的说法，

sentences.en: characters like Chris Traeger are not magical unicorns.
sentences.zh: 像克里斯·特雷格这样的角色并不是魔法独角兽。

sentences.en: They just have a secret.
sentences.zh: 他们只是掌握了一个秘诀。

sentences.en: They are expert at building good habits.
sentences.zh: 他们是培养好习惯的专家。

sentences.en: In her book, Good Habits, Bad Habits, The Science of Making Positive Changes That Stick,
sentences.zh: 在她的大作《好习惯，坏习惯：建立能持久的积极改变的科学》中，

sentences.en: Wendy argues that we can all become experts at building good habits and dismantling bad ones
sentences.zh: 温迪认为，只要我们停下来去理解日常行为背后的心理学，

sentences.en: if we only stop to understand the psychology behind our routines.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都可以成为培养好习惯和打破坏习惯的专家。

sentences.en: Wendy, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 温迪，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm thrilled to be here.
sentences.zh: 哦，我很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: I want to start with something that you once saw on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我想从你曾在脸书上看到的一件事开始讲起。

sentences.en: Your cousin went on Facebook and announced that she was going to change her life,
sentences.zh: 你的表妹在脸书上发文宣布她要改变生活，

sentences.en: by which she meant she wanted to lose some weight.
sentences.zh: 她的意思是她想减减肥。

sentences.en: Why did she announce this on Facebook?
sentences.zh: 她为什么要在这个社交平台上宣布这件事？

sentences.en: And what was the reaction she garnered from her friends?
sentences.zh: 她朋友们的反应又是什么？

sentences.en: So I think by making a public statement,
sentences.zh: 所以我想通过公开表态，

sentences.en: she was trying to commit herself to the initial idea, her initial desire to lose weight.
sentences.zh: 她是在试图让自己对最初的想法——她最初想要减肥的愿望——做出承诺。

sentences.en: In a way, she sort of upped the stakes because she made it public.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，她因为公开表态而提高了赌注。

sentences.en: And then she was accountable to all of her Facebook friends.
sentences.zh: 然后她对所有的脸书好友负起了责任。

sentences.en: And they were highly supportive.
sentences.zh: 他们给予了极大的支持。

sentences.en: They spurred her on and told her how strong she was.
sentences.zh: 他们鼓舞她，告诉她她有多坚强。

sentences.en: So she got a lot of positive reinforcement for that.
sentences.zh: 因此，她为此获得了大量的积极正向反馈。

sentences.en: And the feedback from her friends, this idea of encouraging her, telling her, just do it,
sentences.zh: 朋友们的反馈，这种鼓励她、告诉她“只管去做”的想法，

sentences.en: you know, that reminds me of a video made by the actor Shia LaBeouf.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这让我想起演员希亚·拉博夫制作的一段视频。

sentences.en: He stands in front of a green screen and he says,
sentences.zh: 他站在绿幕前说，

sentences.en: actually, let me just play for you what he says.
sentences.zh: 实际上，让我直接播给大家听听他是怎么说的。

sentences.en: Take a listen.
sentences.zh: 听听看。

sentences.en: Yesterday, you said tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 昨天，你说是明天。

sentences.en: So just do it.
sentences.zh: 所以只管去做。

sentences.en: Make your dreams come true.
sentences.zh: 让你的梦想成真。

sentences.en: You just do it.
sentences.zh: 你只管去做。

sentences.en: This message, Wendy, is so pervasive when it comes to making changes in our life.
sentences.zh: 温迪，当涉及到改变我们的生活时，这种信息是如此无处不在。

sentences.en: The idea that if you want to make a change, all you have to do is just say, just do it.
sentences.zh: 那种认为如果你想做出改变，你所要做的就是说一句“只管去做”的想法。

sentences.en: Wouldn't that be wonderful?
sentences.zh: 那不是很棒吗？

sentences.en: I don't think that's most of our experience.
sentences.zh: 我认为这并不是我们大多数人的经历。

sentences.en: But what we do believe is if we wanted to enough, we'd exert enough willpower and we'd make it happen.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实相信，如果我们渴望得足够强烈，就会施展足够的意志力，从而让它发生。

sentences.en: And the result, though, is that it doesn't often, because willpower is not actually, we have found,
sentences.zh: 然而结果往往并非如此，因为我们发现，意志力实际上并不是

sentences.en: the best way to achieve our goals and to change our behavior.
sentences.zh: 实现我们的目标和改变行为的最佳途径。

sentences.en: Talk about this idea, Wendy, that significant numbers of Americans believe that the way to change their behavior is through self-control,
sentences.zh: 温迪，谈谈这个观点吧：相当多的美国人认为改变行为的途径是通过自我控制，

sentences.en: that willpower is the key to either making changes that stick or to making changes that fail to stick.
sentences.zh: 意志力是实现持久改变或避免半途而废的关键。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's something that pervades our culture.
sentences.zh: 是的，这种观念充斥着我们的文化。

sentences.en: When surveys are done of Americans and their beliefs about how to change behavior, particularly something like obesity,
sentences.zh: 当对美国人及其关于如何改变行为（尤其是像肥胖这样的话题）的信念进行调查时，

sentences.en: three-quarters of Americans think that it's a problem with self-control and willpower, that we just don't have enough.
sentences.zh: 四分之三的美国人认为这是一个自我控制和意志力的问题，也就是我们拥有的还不够多。

sentences.en: And if we had more, we'd all be thinner.
sentences.zh: 如果我们有更多意志力，我们都会变瘦。

sentences.en: Now, researchers have actually looked at this question and asked how much willpower is central.
sentences.zh: 现在，研究人员实际上已经审视了这个问题，并探究了意志力处于何种核心地位。

sentences.en: You cite the work of the late, great psychologist Daniel Wegner, who once ran a study where he told people not to think about a white bear.
sentences.zh: 你引用了已故伟大的心理学家丹尼尔·韦格纳的著作，他曾做过一项研究，让人们不要去想一头白熊。

sentences.en: Why did he do that and what did he find?
sentences.zh: 他为什么要这么做？他发现了什么？

sentences.en: He did it to show that if you try not to think about something, even something as trivial as a white bear that you wouldn't normally think about,
sentences.zh: 他这样做是为了证明，如果你试图不去想某件事，哪怕是一件像白熊这样你平时根本不会去想的琐事，

sentences.en: then later, when you're given an opportunity to think about it again, you just can't stop.
sentences.zh: 那么后来，当你有机会再次去想它时，你简直停不下来。

sentences.en: It's a white bear, white bear, white bear.
sentences.zh: 脑子里全是白熊、白熊、白熊。

sentences.en: So this tells us something about what it's like to try to repress or control our desires.
sentences.zh: 这向我们揭示了试图压抑或控制我们的欲望是怎样一种体验。

sentences.en: Yes, we can do it in the short run, but ultimately it backfires.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在短期内可以做到，但最终会适得其反。

sentences.en: Those ideas get a life of their own and they start to obsess us.
sentences.zh: 那些想法会产生它们自己的生命力，并开始让我们着迷。

sentences.en: And when you think about the behaviors we often want to change in our lives, quitting smoking or eating healthier or exercising more regularly,
sentences.zh: 当你想到我们经常想要改变的生活中的那些行为时，比如戒烟、吃得更健康或更规律地锻炼，

sentences.en: the challenge, of course, is not to make a one-time change, not to exercise well just today.
sentences.zh: 当然，挑战不在于做出一次性的改变，不在于今天锻炼得很好。

sentences.en: The challenge, of course, is to make a long-term change.
sentences.zh: 当然，挑战在于做出长期的改变。

sentences.en: And the research would then suggest that willpower might not be the most effective way to go about achieving that.
sentences.zh: 因此，研究表明，意志力可能并不是实现这一目标的最高效方法。

sentences.en: Yes, that's actually how I got into this whole research area.
sentences.zh: 是的，这其实就是我涉足整个研究领域的契机。

sentences.en: I was interested in understanding what it is that helps people persiSt.
sentences.zh: 我有兴趣了解是什么在帮助人们坚持下去。

sentences.en: So how do people persist at, say, eating healthfully or saving more money or getting more sleep?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们是如何在诸如健康饮食、存更多钱或获得充足睡眠这些事情上坚持不懈的呢？

sentences.en: We can all do this one time or two times, but it's a very different thing to do it on a consistent basis.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都能做这一两次，但要持续不断地做到这一点则是完全不同的另一回事。

sentences.en: When I first started this research, the idea was that we did these things when we were sufficiently committed,
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始这项研究时，当时的观点是我们只有在足够投入的时候才会做这些事情，

sentences.en: when we had enough self-control to follow through.
sentences.zh: 当我们有足够的自控力去贯彻执行时。

sentences.en: Then we'd form these strong intentions and we'd act on them over time.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会形成强烈的意图，并在一段时间内付诸行动。

sentences.en: But I'd noticed that it didn't really play out that way in my life.
sentences.zh: 但我注意到，在我的生活中事情并不是这样发展的。

sentences.en: I've often made decisions that I didn't follow through with, even though I was initially very committed to those decisions.
sentences.zh: 我经常做出最终没有贯彻到底的决定，尽管我最初对这些决定非常投入。

sentences.en: And I have a pretty good amount of willpower.
sentences.zh: 而且我拥有相当可观的意志力。

sentences.en: So what we did is we did a large review of the research to test whether people's decision-making was important
sentences.zh: 所以我们做的是，对相关研究进行了广泛的回顾，以测试人们的决策制定是否重要

sentences.en: all the way through behavior change process, not just from the beginning, where my cousin started on Facebook,
sentences.zh: 贯穿整个行为改变过程的始终，不仅从我表妹在脸书上开始的起点，

sentences.en: declaring she's going to change, but also two, three months later.
sentences.zh: 也就是她宣布自己要改变的时候，而且在两三个月后依然如此。

sentences.en: And what we found was really surprising.
sentences.zh: 而我们的发现真的令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Decision-making, our intentions, our thoughts, our commitment, they're very important when we start to change.
sentences.zh: 决策制定、我们的意图、我们的想法、我们的承诺，在开始改变时非常重要。

sentences.en: That's what determines whether we do behaviors once in a while, continuing over time, took something very different.
sentences.zh: 这决定了我们是否会偶尔做出某些行为，而要长期持续下去则需要完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: And we didn't know what it was to start off with.
sentences.zh: 而且一开始我们并不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: It was like once you start performing a behavior, it just sort of continues on its own.
sentences.zh: 这就好像一旦你开始执行某种行为，它就会自动继续下去。

sentences.en: It's like action begets action.
sentences.zh: 就像行动催生行动。

sentences.en: And what we decided was this is kind of like driving your car, right?
sentences.zh: 我们得出的结论是，这有点像开车，对吧？

sentences.en: So every once in a while, you do pay attention and make decisions.
sentences.zh: 所以偶尔你确实会集中注意力并做出决定。

sentences.en: But most of the time when you're driving, it's sort of in the background.
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候当你开车时，它有点处于背景状态。

sentences.en: You're thinking about something other than what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 你在想别的事情，而不是正在做的事情。

sentences.en: Your actual responses don't take much thought and decision.
sentences.zh: 你实际的反应不需要太多思考和决定。

sentences.en: They're certainly not taking your willpower.
sentences.zh: 它们肯定不需要消耗你的意志力。

sentences.en: It's a counterintuitive idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个反直觉的想法。

sentences.en: Conscious willpower is not the driving force behind sustained behavior change.
sentences.zh: 有意识的意志力并不是持续行为改变背后的驱动力。

sentences.en: That idea is powerfully illustrated by an experiment conducted in Germany that asked two simple questions.
sentences.zh: 德国进行的一项实验有力地说明了这一点，该实验提出了两个简单的问题。

sentences.en: Are people who stick to their resolutions the people who see lots of temptations but have the willpower to resist them?
sentences.zh: 那些坚持目标的人，是那些看到很多诱惑但有意志力去抵制它们的人吗？

sentences.en: Or are they the kind of people who've set up their lives so they don't even notice the temptations?
sentences.zh: 还是那种把生活安排好、甚至注意不到诱惑的人？

sentences.en: They found that contrary to all of our expectations, that people who are high achievers, who we think of as having good willpower, good self-control,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，与我们所有的预期相反，那些成就很高、我们认为意志力很好、自控力很好的人，

sentences.en: they didn't actually experience many temptations.
sentences.zh: 他们其实并没有经历太多的诱惑。

sentences.en: They weren't conflicted by having lots of desires that were inappropriate and things they didn't want to do.
sentences.zh: 他们不会因为有许多不恰当的欲望和不想做的事情而感到内心冲突。

sentences.en: That was the people who were low in self-control, the people who weren't that successful at achieving their goals in life.
sentences.zh: 那是自控力较低的人，也就是那些在生活中实现目标不太成功的人。

sentences.en: In other words, this is not a case of people who have cake in the refrigerator and are very good at resisting opening the refrigerator to eat the cake.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这不是冰箱里有蛋糕、并且很擅长忍住不去打开冰箱吃蛋糕的人的情况。

sentences.en: These are just people who don't have cake in the refrigerator.
sentences.zh: 这些人只是冰箱里没有蛋糕而已。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Or if they do, they don't see it.
sentences.zh: 或者如果有的话，他们也看不见。

sentences.en: They have coded that as, okay, that's my kid's cake.
sentences.zh: 他们已经将其编码为：好吧，那是给我孩子吃的蛋糕。

sentences.en: I don't eat that.
sentences.zh: 我不吃那个。

sentences.en: I eat the fruit.
sentences.zh: 我吃水果。

sentences.en: And I like the fruit.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢水果。

sentences.en: How do they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: It turns out that when you build a habit, it's like putting on a set of unconscious mental blinders.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，当你养成习惯时，就像戴上了一副无意识的心智眼罩。

sentences.en: Once in place, the blinders protect you from temptations and distractions.
sentences.zh: 一旦戴上，眼罩就能保护你免受诱惑和干扰。

sentences.en: The more you ignore those temptations, the stronger the blinders become.
sentences.zh: 你越是忽视这些诱惑，眼罩就会变得越强大。

sentences.en: To put this another way, habits are self-reinforcing.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，习惯具有自我强化的作用。

sentences.en: They can be difficult to start, but once in place, they have a life of their own because they stop being conscious and become automatic and unconscious.
sentences.zh: 它们可能很难开始，但一旦形成，就会拥有自己的生命，因为它们不再是有意识的，而是变得自动化和无意识的。

sentences.en: In fact, once you have developed a habit, you will stick to it even if the alternative is objectively easier.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一旦你养成了习惯，即使替代方案在客观上更容易，你也会坚持它。

sentences.en: Wendy has a nice example of this from her own life.
sentences.zh: 温迪用她自己生活中的一个例子很好地说明了这一点。

sentences.en: She sometimes goes biking with a friend who's a professional cycliSt.
sentences.zh: 她有时会和一位身为职业自行车手的女性朋友一起骑车。

sentences.en: Yeah, so she and I were good friends, and we'd love to talk about our families and just exchange information about our lives.
sentences.zh: 对，所以她和我是好朋友，我们喜欢谈论我们的家庭，只交流关于我们生活的信息。

sentences.en: And that would happen as we started the bike ride.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始骑自行车时就会这样。

sentences.en: Now, she's a professional cyclist, so you might wonder what she's doing riding with me.
sentences.zh: 现在，她是一名职业自行车手，所以你可能会好奇她在和我一起骑车时在做什么。

sentences.en: Well, I rode with her on her days off when she was supposed to be just not breaking a sweat.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我和她一起骑车是在她的休息日，那时她本来应该是不流汗的轻松骑行。

sentences.en: And that was fine, you know, because that's the speed I ride at.
sentences.zh: 这很好，你知道的，因为那是我的骑行速度。

sentences.en: But, and so we'd have a good time talking and chatting.
sentences.zh: 而且，所以我们聊得很开心。

sentences.en: And then after we'd been cycling for maybe an hour and a half, she would start speeding up.
sentences.zh: 然后，当我们骑了一个半小时左右之后，她就会开始加速。

sentences.en: And she did this consistently.
sentences.zh: 而且她一直都是这样。

sentences.en: And I tried not to take it personally because, you know, you can't talk to somebody who's cycling that faSt.
sentences.zh: 我尽量不把它放在心上，因为你知道的，你无法和一个骑得那么快的人说话。

sentences.en: And I asked her at the end of one of our rides, so what happens at the end?
sentences.zh: 在一次骑行结束时我问她，最后到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Because, you know, I kind of lose you.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，我有点跟不上你。

sentences.en: And she said, well, I'm just so tired at going at the slow pace.
sentences.zh: 她说，嗯，以这么慢的速度骑我实在是太累了。

sentences.en: I can't control my actions any more.
sentences.zh: 我无法再控制自己的行为了。

sentences.en: And I just naturally speed up.
sentences.zh: 我自然而然地就加速了。

sentences.en: So what this indicates, I think it's a fascinating example because it indicates that the habit is not necessarily the easiest thing or the low effort thing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这表明，我认为这是一个引人入胜的例子，因为它表明习惯不一定是做起来最容易或最省力的事情。

sentences.en: Instead, it's what you usually do that you fall back on.
sentences.zh: 相反，它是你通常所做的、你会退而求其次去做的事。

sentences.en: There have been anecdotal accounts of how long it takes to develop a habit.
sentences.zh: 关于养成一个习惯需要多长时间，有一些轶事记载。

sentences.en: And you and others have had the insight that this number is probably not the same for different kinds of habits, that some habits in some ways are easier to form than others.
sentences.zh: 你和其他人都有这样一种深刻见解：对于不同种类的习惯，这个数字可能并不相同，有些习惯在某些方面比其他习惯更容易形成。

sentences.en: Perhaps they have larger rewards than others.
sentences.zh: 也许它们的回报比其他习惯更大。

sentences.en: What does the science tell us about how long it takes to develop different habits like exercising or writing or going to the gym?
sentences.zh: 科学告诉我们，养成锻炼、写作或去健身房等不同习惯需要多长时间？

sentences.en: Habits are cognitive associations.
sentences.zh: 习惯是认知联结。

sentences.en: They're mental associations that we form when we repeat an action over and over again in a given context and then get a reward.
sentences.zh: 它们是我们在特定情境下重复采取某种行动并获得回报时形成的心理联结。

sentences.en: When you do that, you are learning very slowly and incrementally to associate that context with that behavior.
sentences.zh: 当你这样做时，你是在非常缓慢且循序渐进地学习将该情境与该行为联系起来。

sentences.en: So the next time you're in that context, the behavior automatically comes to mind.
sentences.zh: 所以下次你处于那种情境时，该行为就会自动浮现在脑海中。

sentences.en: You might be very consistent in how you repeat an action and I might be more variable.
sentences.zh: 你重复某个行动的方式可能非常一致，而我的方式可能会多变一些。

sentences.en: And if I'm more variable, it's going to take longer to form that habit, that mental association in mind.
sentences.zh: 如果我的方式多变，那么在脑海中形成那种习惯、那种心理联结就需要更长的时间。

sentences.en: But also for complex behaviors, for things that have many different parts, it takes longer to form a habit.
sentences.zh: 但同样，对于复杂的行为，对于有许多不同组成部分的事情，形成习惯需要更长的时间。

sentences.en: And the best evidence we have at this point is from a study that had people add a simple health behavior to their day.
sentences.zh: 我们目前拥有的最好证据来自一项研究，该研究让人们在日常生活中增加了一项简单的健康行为。

sentences.en: Finally, adding something like a glass of water took two months to become automated so that you don't have to make decisions about it.
sentences.zh: 最后，像增加一杯水这样的小事需要两个月的时间才能自动化，这样你就不用为此做决定了。

sentences.en: Something like going to the gym could take three, four months before of going every day before it becomes really habitual in the sense that you don't have to think.
sentences.zh: 像去健身房这样的事情可能需要三、四个月的每天坚持，然后它才会真正成为一种习惯，这意味着你不再需要思考。

sentences.en: You just do.
sentences.zh: 你只是去做。

sentences.en: So one implication of this is that just as you can have good habits that cause you to do things unthinkingly,
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着，正如你可能会拥有让你不假思索地做事的良好习惯一样，

sentences.en: you can also develop bad habits that cause you to do things unthinkingly.
sentences.zh: 你也会养成让你不假思索地做事的坏习惯。

sentences.en: You mentioned another neighbor friend of yours who sometimes has to decide whether to drive to her kid's school or walk to her kid's school.
sentences.zh: 你提到了你的另一位邻居朋友，她有时不得不决定是开车送孩子上学还是走路送孩子上学。

sentences.en: And that reveals something really interesting about the power of habit.
sentences.zh: 这揭示了关于习惯力量的一个非常有趣的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we lived in a small neighborhood and the school was actually right next to her house.
sentences.zh: 所以我们住在一个小社区里，学校实际上就在她家隔壁。

sentences.en: And one night at a parent-teacher conference, I watched her get into her car and drive to the school parking lot,
sentences.zh: 一天晚上在家长会上，我看着她上车并开车去学校停车场，

sentences.en: which was actually further from the front door of the school than her house.
sentences.zh: 那个停车场实际上比她家距离学校正门还要远。

sentences.en: Her habit was to get in the car.
sentences.zh: 她的习惯就是上车。

sentences.en: And this was in Texas.
sentences.zh: 这是在得克萨斯州。

sentences.en: So it was hot.
sentences.zh: 所以很热。

sentences.en: So if she'd been thinking, she would have been very cognizant of the weather and that she was actually going to be uncomfortable for longer if she took her car than if she walked.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果她在思考，她就会非常清楚天气情况，并且知道如果她开车，实际上比走路会感到不舒服更长时间。

sentences.en: There's an underlying subtext to many of these stories.
sentences.zh: 许多这些故事背后都有一个潜在的潜台词。

sentences.en: And that subtext is that in much of our lives, our actions are actually not being driven by conscious and deliberate intention.
sentences.zh: 那个潜台词就是，在我们生活的大部分时间里，我们的行动实际上并不是由有意识和深思熟虑的意图驱动的。

sentences.en: And that's a subtext that runs through much of your book, this idea that much of our lives actually is being run on autopilot.
sentences.zh: 这个潜台词贯穿了你的大部分书，这个观点即我们生活的大部分时间实际上都是在自动驾驶状态下运行的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One of the first studies we did, we tried to figure out what percentage of daily actions are habitual in the way that you describe.
sentences.zh: 我们做的首批研究之一，试图弄清楚日常行动中有多少比例像你所描述的那样具有习惯性。

sentences.en: And what we found is that about 43% of everyday actions are done repeatedly, almost every day in the same context.
sentences.zh: 我们发现大约 43% 的日常行动是重复进行的，几乎每天都在相同的语境下发生。

sentences.en: Again, it's very much like driving.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这非常像开车。

sentences.en: We have this general sense that we're doing things, but it's not driven by an active decision-making process.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种笼统的感觉，觉得自己正在做事情，但它并不是由积极的决策过程驱动的。

sentences.en: So the interesting thing is that because we don't acknowledge or often recognize how powerful these unthinking forces are, in many of our campaigns, our public health campaigns,
sentences.zh: 所以有趣的是，因为我们不承认或经常认识不到这些不假思索的力量有多么强大，在我们许多的活动中，我们的公共健康活动，

sentences.en: for example, we focus primarily on changing people's conscious beliefs and attitudes.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们主要关注改变人们有意识的信念和态度。

sentences.en: And you have some really interesting ideas on how this plays out when it comes to getting people to eat right.
sentences.zh: 对于如何让人门吃得健康这一点，你有一些非常有趣的观点，说明了这一点是如何发挥作用的。

sentences.en: You've looked at, for example, campaigns to get people to eat more fruits and vegetables.
sentences.zh: 例如，你研究过让人门多吃水果和蔬菜的活动。

sentences.en: What do you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, probably one of the most famous campaigns actually started here in California, Five a Day, Eating Five a Day Fruits and Vegetables.
sentences.zh: 是的，实际上最著名的活动之一始于加利福尼亚州，即“每天五份”，每天吃五份水果和蔬菜。

sentences.en: Five a day, eat five a day.
sentences.zh: 每天五份，每天吃五份。

sentences.en: We all know that's the healthy way.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道这是健康的方式。

sentences.en: Fruits and vegetables, they're okay.
sentences.zh: 水果和蔬菜，它们很好。

sentences.en: A healthy way, eat five a day.
sentences.zh: 健康的方式，每天吃五份。

sentences.en: When it began in the 1990s, only 8% of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当它在 20 世纪 90 年代开始时，只有 8% 的美国

sentences.en: population realized that they needed to eat five servings of fruits and vegetables a day.
sentences.zh: 人口意识到他们每天需要吃五份水果和蔬菜。

sentences.en: Five years later, over a third of Americans understood they need to eat five servings of fruits and vegetables a day.
sentences.zh: 五年后，超过三分之一的美国人明白他们需要每天吃五份水果和蔬菜。

sentences.en: But when you look at what people were doing, the campaign looks really different.
sentences.zh: 但当你看看人们的实际做法时，这项活动看起来截然不同。

sentences.en: So before the campaign started, 11% of us were actually eating five servings of fruits and vegetables a day.
sentences.zh: 所以在活动开始前，我们当中只有 11% 的人真的每天吃五份水果和蔬菜。

sentences.en: Ten years later, still 11%.
sentences.zh: 十年后，依然是 11%。

sentences.en: And even more recent assessments have shown that Americans are declining from that point.
sentences.zh: 甚至最近的评估也表明，美国人的这一比例正在下降。

sentences.en: Fewer and fewer of us are eating that amount.
sentences.zh: 我们当中吃这个数量的人越来越少。

sentences.en: And part of the reason for this is much of our eating is habitual.
sentences.zh: 造成这种情况的部分原因是，我们的饮食很大程度上是习惯性的。

sentences.en: We do it automatically.
sentences.zh: 我们自动地进食。

sentences.en: We shop automatically.
sentences.zh: 我们自动地购物。

sentences.en: We only go down certain aisles in the grocery store.
sentences.zh: 我们只走杂货店里的某些过道。

sentences.en: People might not even go down the produce aisle.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至可能不会走进生鲜区。

sentences.en: So they're not going to be influenced by this abstract thought, yes, fruits and vegetables are good for me.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不会受到这种抽象想法的影响，即“是的，水果和蔬菜对我有益”。

sentences.en: Instead, they're eating based on the environment that they're in and the patterns they've developed.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们的饮食取决于他们所处的环境以及他们养成的模式。

sentences.en: I mean, I feel like I see this in so many different campaigns where the idea is if we can change people's beliefs, their behavior will follow.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得我在许多不同的活动中都看到了这一点，其核心理念是如果我们能改变人们的信念，他们的行为就会随之改变。

sentences.en: And, of course, intuitively that's a very appealing idea, but really the evidence doesn't seem to support it.
sentences.zh: 当然，从直觉上看，这是一个非常吸引人的想法，但证据似乎并不支持它。

sentences.en: No, I mean, it does support it for one-off behaviors, limited behaviors, single-time behavior change.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，它确实支持一次性行为、有限行为、单次行为改变。

sentences.en: So if you're trying to get people to sign up for a program, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你试图让人们报名参加一个项目，例如，

sentences.en: then convincing people to do it and giving them the opportunity right when you convince them is probably a pretty effective way to do it.
sentences.zh: 那么说服人们去做并在你游说他们的时候立即给他们提供机会，可能是一种非常有效的方法。

sentences.en: But so many of health behaviors, of financial behaviors, relationships, productivity, these things involve long-term change in behavior.
sentences.zh: 但许多健康行为、财务行为、人际关系、生产力，这些事情都涉及长期的行为改变。

sentences.en: And that you don't get by convincing people to do things.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是靠说服人们做事就能做到的。

sentences.en: So if conscious beliefs and intentions don't get people to change their behavior, how can we use science to start habits or break them?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果有意识的信念和意图无法让人门改变行为，我们如何利用科学来开启或打破习惯？

sentences.en: That's when we come back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Wendy Wood is a professor of psychology and business at the University of Southern California.
sentences.zh: 温迪·伍德是南加州大学的心理学和商学教授。

sentences.en: She says corporations are increasingly drawing on insights about habits to influence their workforce.
sentences.zh: 她说，企业越来越多地利用关于习惯的见解来影响其员工队伍。

sentences.en: One example, Uber.
sentences.zh: 一个例子是优步（Uber）。

sentences.en: Being a driver on Uber is difficult in many ways, right?
sentences.zh: 在优步当司机在很多方面都很困难，对吧？

sentences.en: You're taking your own personal car and you are using it for business.
sentences.zh: 你用的是你自己的私家车，并且把它用于商业用途。

sentences.en: You have a bunch of strangers sitting in the back.
sentences.zh: 后座上坐着一堆陌生人。

sentences.en: So Uber would put a lot of money into training and evaluating drivers and their cars.
sentences.zh: 因此，优步会投入大量资金来培训和评估司机及其车辆。

sentences.en: And then drivers would quit after, well, before they got to 10 rides.
sentences.zh: 然后司机们就会辞职，嗯，在他们完成 10 次行程之前。

sentences.en: And so Uber would lose money.
sentences.zh: 所以优步会亏钱。

sentences.en: So what they decided to do was they decided to automate.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定实现自动化。

sentences.en: And you've probably heard this, when you're in an Uber, at the end of your ride, the phone app pings and then assigns the driver to the next ride.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过，当你坐在优步车里时，在行程结束时，手机应用会响铃，然后将司机分配到下一次行程。

sentences.en: So they don't have time to think and maybe decide, OK, this is getting difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有时间去思考并可能决定：“好吧，这变得很困难。我要回家了。”

sentences.en: I'm going home.
sentences.zh: 我要回家了。

sentences.en: They're off on their next ride.
sentences.zh: 他们已经踏上了下一次行程。

sentences.en: And so it moves them forward through the process to the point where they start feeling more comfortable with what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 这推动他们在整个过程中前进，直到他们开始对所做的事情感到更加适应。

sentences.en: And they can develop some habitual patterns of dealing with customers.
sentences.zh: 并且他们可以培养出一些与客户打交道的习惯性模式。

sentences.en: So there's an important insight here.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个重要的见解。

sentences.en: And this is an insight that's useful not just for, you know, a multibillion-dollar business trying to manipulate the behavior of its workforce.
sentences.zh: 这个见解不仅对那些试图操纵员工行为的价值数十亿美元的企业有用，

sentences.en: But it's an insight that affects all of us.
sentences.zh: 而且这个见解影响着我们所有人。

sentences.en: You know, when I'm sitting on my couch and I'm watching Netflix, at the end of each episode of Netflix, I don't actually have to press any buttons.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我坐在沙发上观看 Netflix 时，在 Netflix 的每一集结束时，我实际上不需要按任何按钮。

sentences.en: Netflix tells me in nine seconds the next episode is going to start.
sentences.zh: Netflix 会在九秒钟内告诉我下一集即将开始。

sentences.en: And that's really the same idea as what Uber is doing to its drivers.
sentences.zh: 这实际上与优步对其司机所做的事情是同一个想法。

sentences.en: It's basically saying you can change people's behavior by essentially making it frictionless for them to keep doing the behavior.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是在说，你可以通过本质上消除他们继续某种行为的阻力来改变人们的行为。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that is essentially what most commercial industries have figured out how to do at this point in one way or another.
sentences.zh: 这本质上就是大多数商业行业目前已经以这样或那样的方式弄清楚如何做的事情。

sentences.en: Will you have fries with that is probably the classic example of encouraging certain behaviors, making behaviors easy, consumption, spending money.
sentences.zh: “要来份薯条吗？”大概是鼓励某些行为、使行为变得容易、促进消费和花钱的经典例子。

sentences.en: You can think of so many examples of this in our modern culture.
sentences.zh: 在我们的现代文化中，你可以想到无数这样的例子。

sentences.en: I wonder if we can take this insight, Wendy, and apply it to how you can actually start to build habits.
sentences.zh: 温迪，我想知道我们是否可以将这个见解应用到如何真正开始培养习惯上。

sentences.en: So in exactly the same way that corporations in some ways manipulate us into doing what they want us to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像某些情况下企业操纵我们去做他们想让我们做的事情一样，

sentences.en: I want to explore how we might be able to manipulate ourselves into doing things that we think are good for us.
sentences.zh: 我想探讨我们如何才能操纵自己去做那些我们认为对自己有益的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So we all know that people are most likely to repeat actions that are easy for them and actions that are fun.
sentences.zh: 所以我们都知道，人们最容易重复那些对他们来说简单且有趣的行为。

sentences.en: So if you really don't like going to the gym, then you're not going to do it very often.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你真的很不喜欢去健身房，那你肯定不会经常去。

sentences.en: And you need to figure out something to do to make it more fun.
sentences.zh: 你得想点办法让它变得更有趣。

sentences.en: Making it easy is also critical.
sentences.zh: 让过程变简单也至关重要。

sentences.en: So there is a study that is quite amazing, I think, but it has been replicated a couple of times, on how far people travel to the gym.
sentences.zh: 有一项研究我认为非常惊艳，而且已经被复制了好几次，关于人们为了去健身房愿意走多远。

sentences.en: If people travel about three and a half miles, then they are likely to go to the gym five times a month on average.
sentences.zh: 如果人们路程在大约三英里半左右，那么他们平均一个月可能会去五次健身房。

sentences.en: If people travel five miles, then they're likely to go only once a month on average.
sentences.zh: 如果路程是五英里，那么他们平均一个月可能只会去一次。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The five miles presents friction.
sentences.zh: 五英里的距离带来了阻力。

sentences.en: The 3.5 miles is much less friction and makes the behavior more likely.
sentences.zh: 3.5英里的阻力要小得多，也更容易促成这种行为。

sentences.en: We just don't have to struggle so much to get there.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要费那么大劲去到那里。

sentences.en: And anything that reduces the struggle and the stress is going to make habits more likely to form.
sentences.zh: 任何能减少阻力和压力的事情，都会让习惯更容易养成。

sentences.en: I don't know if you noticed this, but Wendy and I have mentioned a specific word a couple of times in the last few minutes.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有注意到，但温迪和我在过去几分钟里已经多次提到过一个特定的词。

sentences.en: Friction.
sentences.zh: 阻力。

sentences.en: When things are difficult to do, they have high friction.
sentences.zh: 当事情做起来很困难时，它们的阻力就很大。

sentences.en: When doing something is effortless, there's low friction.
sentences.zh: 当做某事不费吹灰之力时，阻力就很小。

sentences.en: It turns out this word is incredibly important to understand how habits work.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这个词对于理解习惯是如何运作的极其重要。

sentences.en: One unusual study revealed the power of friction using stale popcorn.
sentences.zh: 一项不同寻常的研究利用陈旧的爆米花揭示了阻力的力量。

sentences.en: We did it in a local movie theater.
sentences.zh: 我们在当地的一家电影院做了这个实验。

sentences.en: We had the movie patrons watch a bunch of trailers and rate them for us.
sentences.zh: 我们让电影观众观看了一堆预告片并为它们打分。

sentences.en: This summer, experience the love of the world's greatest athlete.
sentences.zh: 这个夏天，体验世界上最伟大运动员的爱。

sentences.en: Every day, millions of people go through the same routine while life passes them by.
sentences.zh: 每一天，数以百万计的人在生活中日复一日地重复着同样的日常。

sentences.en: Coming soon for a cinema.
sentences.zh: 即将上映。

sentences.en: And supposedly, as compensation, we gave them boxes of popcorn to eat.
sentences.zh: 据推测，作为报酬，我们送了他们一盒盒爆米花吃。

sentences.en: Now, unbeknownst to them, some got stale popcorn, which we had popped earlier and kept in our lab for a week in a plastic bag.
sentences.zh: 现在，在他们不知情的情况下，有些人拿到了陈旧的爆米花，这是我们早些时候爆好并放在实验室塑料袋里存了一个星期的。

sentences.en: So it was pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 所以味道相当糟糕。

sentences.en: And others got boxes of fresh popcorn.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人则拿到了新鲜的爆米花。

sentences.en: And what we found was this, that people who don't eat popcorn regularly in the movie theater did just what you'd expect.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是：那些平时不在电影院吃爆米花的人，表现正如你所料。

sentences.en: They ate a lot of the fresh popcorn, the stale popcorn they just avoided.
sentences.zh: 他们吃了很多新鲜的爆米花，而陈旧的爆米花他们根本不碰。

sentences.en: What was most interesting, though, are the people, the movie patrons, who often ate popcorn in the movie theater.
sentences.zh: 然而，最有趣的是那些经常在电影院吃爆米花的观众。

sentences.en: They ate 70% of these boxes, whether they were fresh or stale.
sentences.zh: 无论新鲜还是陈旧，他们都吃掉了这些盒子里70%的爆米花。

sentences.en: Now, what's so surprising is we asked them afterwards how much they liked the popcorn.
sentences.zh: 让人惊奇的是，我们事后问他们有多喜欢这些爆米花。

sentences.en: And they could all tell us they hated the stale popcorn.
sentences.zh: 他们都能告诉我们他们讨厌陈旧的爆米花。

sentences.en: But to people who have habits, the cues are so, so strong in that particular context that they just respond to them without thinking.
sentences.zh: 但对于有习惯的人来说，在特定情境下的暗示是如此之强烈，以至于他们不经思考就会做出反应。

sentences.en: And they get the stale popcorn in their mouth and they think, oh, okay, that wasn't great.
sentences.zh: 当他们把陈旧的爆米花放进嘴里时，他们会想，哦，好吧，这味道不太妙。

sentences.en: But then, before they know it, they're back to eating again.
sentences.zh: 但随后，不知不觉中，他们又开始吃了。

sentences.en: That same stuff that they don't like.
sentences.zh: 吃那些他们明明不喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: Wendy added an interesting twist to the study.
sentences.zh: 温迪给这项研究加入了一个有趣的转折。

sentences.en: And this is the part where friction comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是阻力发挥作用的部分。

sentences.en: She ran the same experiment, except this time she got right-handed volunteers to eat the popcorn with their left hand
sentences.zh: 她重复了同样的实验，只是这一次她让右利手志愿者用左手吃爆米花，

sentences.en: and left-handed volunteers to eat with their right hand.
sentences.zh: 让左利手志愿者用右手吃。

sentences.en: And that's not something that most of us do on a regular basis.
sentences.zh: 这并不是我们大多数人平时会做的事。

sentences.en: So it made the eating more thoughtful.
sentences.zh: 所以这让吃爆米花的过程变得需要动脑筋了。

sentences.en: If you add that thought to the behavior, you make people attend to it,
sentences.zh: 如果你把这种思考加入到行为中，让人们去关注它，

sentences.en: then our strong habit participants quit eating the stale popcorn.
sentences.zh: 那么我们那些习惯强烈的参与者就停止吃陈旧的爆米花 了。

sentences.en: It's as if if they had to think about it, they realized, oh, this stuff really tastes bad.
sentences.zh: 就好像他们一旦需要思考，就会意识到，哦，这东西味道确实很糟。

sentences.en: And so I'm not going to eat it anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以我再也不吃了。

sentences.en: So in some ways, if I could put this another way, is one of the insights of your work that if you want to build something into a habit,
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，如果换一种说法，你工作的一个核心见解是：如果你想把某种东西培养成习惯，

sentences.en: you actually want to try and make it as unconscious and as automatic as possible.
sentences.zh: 你其实应该尽量让它变得越无意识、越自动化越好。

sentences.en: And if you want to interrupt a bad habit, you might want to find ways to try and make it just a little bit more conscious,
sentences.zh: 而如果你想打破一个坏习惯，你可能需要找方法让它变得稍微更有意识一点，

sentences.en: try to be a little bit more mindful of the habit as you're actually performing it.
sentences.zh: 在实际执行这个习惯时，试着对它保持多一点的觉察。

sentences.en: Is that an insight that would come away from your work?
sentences.zh: 这是从你的研究中得出的一个见解吗？

sentences.en: Yes, yes, I think I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: And we see people all around us who do those things or don't.
sentences.zh: 我们看到身边的人有的在这样做，有的则没有。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So people who are very successful as writers, as athletes, they are people who have made the repetition automatic and they do it every day.
sentences.zh: 所以那些在写作、体育方面非常成功的人，他们都是把重复动作自动化并且每天都在做的人。

sentences.en: You know, you hear about famous writers turning out certain numbers of pages a day, writing for a certain amount of time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你听说过某些著名的作家每天写出一定数量的页数，坚持写作一定的时间。

sentences.en: Athletes work out for certain periods every day.
sentences.zh: 运动员每天锻炼一定的时间。

sentences.en: These people have automated the hard work.
sentences.zh: 这些人已经把艰苦的工作自动化了。

sentences.en: Doesn't make it doesn't mean that they're not working hard, but they've made it easier for themselves to do that.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着他们没有努力工作，而是他们让自己更容易做到这一点。

sentences.en: If you want to make it more difficult to do something, you want to stop yourself, then you figure out ways to add friction to the behaviors that you don't want to engage in.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让某项行为变得更困难，想要阻止自己，那么你会想方设法给你不想去做的行为增加阻力。

sentences.en: That makes you stop and think and perhaps gives you a bit of a chance to realize, oh, this is not really what I intended.
sentences.zh: 这会让你停下来思考，或许能给你一个机会去意识到，哦，这其实不是我的本意。

sentences.en: Maybe I can do something better.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以做得更好。

sentences.en: You were at a conference in Europe one time and you use the power of friction to get people to eat more fruit.
sentences.zh: 你曾在欧洲参加过一个会议，并利用阻力的力量让人多吃水果。

sentences.en: What did you do, Wendy?
sentences.zh: 你做了什么，温迪？

sentences.en: Oh, well, this was actually a conference that I run on habits on Catalina Island here in California.
sentences.zh: 哦，这个嘛，这其实是我在加州卡特琳娜岛上主持的一个关于习惯的会议。

sentences.en: But we had that year a bunch of European participants.
sentences.zh: 但那一年我们有一群欧洲参与者。

sentences.en: And I've noticed that Europeans eat lots of fruit.
sentences.zh: 我注意到欧洲人吃很多水果。

sentences.en: So I ordered extra fruit for them.
sentences.zh: 所以我为他们订购了额外的水果。

sentences.en: But the cafeteria folks had put the fruit in a box that was just to the side of the cafeteria line and no one was eating it.
sentences.zh: 但自助餐厅的工作人员把水果放在了一个刚好在自助餐队伍旁边的盒子里，结果谁也没吃。

sentences.en: And I noticed it.
sentences.zh: 我注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: So I put it right in the middle of the line and it went immediately.
sentences.zh: 所以我把它直接放在了队伍正中间，结果瞬间就被抢光了。

sentences.en: By then, the bananas were a little brownish, but they still, it was obvious and people, I had made it easy and obvious how to get the fruit.
sentences.zh: 当时香蕉有点发褐，但大家还是能看到，我让获取水果变得既简单又显眼。

sentences.en: People ate it.
sentences.zh: 人们都吃了。

sentences.en: In many ways, this is the same insight of the irresistible staircase in Seattle.
sentences.zh: 从很多方面来看，这与西雅图那个无法抗拒的楼梯有异曲同工之妙。

sentences.en: The architects hid the elevators out of sight by placing the stairs front and center, by making their use frictionless.
sentences.zh: 建筑师将电梯藏在视线之外，把楼梯放在正前方和中央，消除了使用楼梯的阻力。

sentences.en: The building made it more likely people would unconsciously choose the path of least resistance and climb the stairs.
sentences.zh: 这栋建筑使得人们更有可能在无意识中选择阻力最小的路径并爬楼梯。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to build our own versions of the irresistible staircase?
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨如何打造我们自己的“无法抗拒的楼梯”。

sentences.en: We'll look at more ways that we can use friction and other tools to change our habits.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨更多利用阻力和其他工具来改变习惯的方法。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请不要走开。

sentences.en: There is a reason many of us form bad habits.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人养成坏习惯是有原因的。

sentences.en: Things like smoking or gambling have long-term negative consequences, but they're extremely rewarding in the short term.
sentences.zh: 吸烟或赌博之类的事情会带来长期的负面后果，但它们在短期内能提供极大的奖赏。

sentences.en: Wendy says habits are powerfully shaped by short-term rewards.
sentences.zh: 温迪说，习惯在很大程度上是由短期奖赏塑造的。

sentences.en: This has to do with the reward component of habits.
sentences.zh: 这与习惯中的奖赏机制有关。

sentences.en: So, what we know about rewards is that our brain responds with dopamine when we get rewarded,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们对奖赏的了解是，当我们得到奖赏时，我们的大脑会释放多巴胺，

sentences.en: and that dopamine is what helps to build the mental associations of habit in our brain.
sentences.zh: 正是这种多巴胺帮助我们在大脑中建立起习惯的精神联结。

sentences.en: And this means that only certain types of rewards are really going to be useful in forming habits, and they're the rewards you experience immediately.
sentences.zh: 这意味着只有某些类型的奖赏才能真正对形成习惯有用，那就是你立即能体验到的奖赏。

sentences.en: Things like exercising or eating healthy food often have tremendous long-term benefits, but they're often not very fun to do.
sentences.zh: 诸如锻炼或吃健康食品之类的事情往往有巨大的长期益处，但做起来通常没那么有趣。

sentences.en: No surprise, they don't produce the quick dopamine bursts.
sentences.zh: 毫不意外，它们不会产生快速的多巴胺爆发。

sentences.en: So, how do you form habits around healthy behaviors?
sentences.zh: 那么，如何围绕健康行为养成习惯呢？

sentences.en: You have to consciously figure out ways to link these healthy behaviors with short-term rewards.
sentences.zh: 你必须有意识地想办法将这些健康行为与短期奖赏联系起来。

sentences.en: Don't just force yourself to eat more veggies.
sentences.zh: 不要只是强迫自己多吃蔬菜。

sentences.en: Figure out ways to make the veggies delicious and enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 要想方设法把蔬菜做得美味可口。

sentences.en: So, if when you eat vegetables, if you really like the taste of beautifully cooked vegetables, and you feel pride in eating healthfully and taking care of yourself,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在吃蔬菜时真的很喜欢精心烹制蔬菜的味道，并且为健康饮食和照顾自己感到骄傲，

sentences.en: those are immediate rewards, and they will help you build a habit.
sentences.zh: 这些就是即时奖赏，它们将帮助你养成习惯。

sentences.en: If your reward is some bonus at the end of the week, or something that you give yourself for achieving, say, some health goal several months down the road,
sentences.zh: 如果你的奖赏是周末结束时的某种奖金，或是你为实现某个几个月后的健康目标而给予自己的某种奖励，

sentences.en: that's not going to be the kind of reward that builds a habit, because it's not there when you are acting.
sentences.zh: 那将不会成为那种能建立习惯的奖赏，因为它在你行动时并不存在。

sentences.en: So, there's an interesting implication of this, and in some ways it's a sad implication, which is when you think about it,
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一个有趣的推论，从某种角度来说这也是一个令人沮丧的推论，仔细想想的话，

sentences.en: this explains why it's easy to form a habit of eating dessert or smoking or drinking, because the rewards when you do those things are relatively quick.
sentences.zh: 这就解释了为什么养成吃甜点、抽烟或喝酒的习惯很容易，因为当你做这些事情时，奖赏是相对迅速的。

sentences.en: An exercise routine or a healthy diet, these are not things where you see the benefit for very long periods of time, unless, as you say,
sentences.zh: 而锻炼计划或健康的饮食，你并不能在很长的一段时间内看到它们的好处，除非，正如你所说，

sentences.en: you develop these intrinsic systems to feel pride as you're doing something.
sentences.zh: 你在做事时培养了这种产生自豪感的内在系统。

sentences.en: Not just waiting for the reward three months or three years down the line.
sentences.zh: 而不是苦等三个月或三年后的奖赏。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But you have a little bit more control than that, because you can add things to behaviors that might not be intrinsically rewarding to you initially.
sentences.zh: 但你可以有更多的掌控力，因为你可以在那些最初可能无法给你带来内在奖赏的行为中加入一些东西。

sentences.en: As I said, you can listen to good music when you work out.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，你可以在锻炼时听好听的音乐。

sentences.en: I hate to admit this, I work out on elliptical some days, and that's probably the most boring thing you can do in the world.
sentences.zh: 我很不愿意承认这一点，我有时会在椭圆机上锻炼，那可能是世界上最无聊的事情了。

sentences.en: So, I watch competitive cooking shows when I do it, and I only let myself watch those shows when I'm on the elliptical.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在锻炼时会看竞技烹饪节目，而且我只允许自己在踩椭圆机时看这些节目。

sentences.en: So, that's my reward for working out, and it's made it into quite a pleasurable habit, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我锻炼的奖赏，事实上，它已经变成了一个非常令人愉快的习惯。

sentences.en: Tell me about your own efforts to become a regular or habitual jogger.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲你自己成为一名定期或习惯性慢跑者的努力经历。

sentences.en: How did that work?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: What were the obstacles you faced, and how did you try and devise methods to overcome them?
sentences.zh: 你面监过什么障碍，你又是如何设计方法去克服它们的？

sentences.en: Oh, this is when my sons were young.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是我的儿子们还小的时候。

sentences.en: I have two sons, two years apart in age, and I had a full-time job, and a husband who had a full-time job.
sentences.zh: 我有两个儿子，年龄相差两岁，我当时有一份全职工作，我丈夫也有一份全职工作。

sentences.en: So, that was a bit of a challenge to find any time to exercise or do anything else.
sentences.zh: 所以，要找时间锻炼或做点别的确实是个不小的挑战。

sentences.en: And that was a real challenge for me early on.
sentences.zh: 这对我早期来说是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: For about five years, I struggled trying to figure that out.
sentences.zh: 在大约五年的时间里，我一直在艰难地摸索。

sentences.en: If you have little kids, you know, you say, I'm going to work out today at 4 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 如果你有小孩，你知道的，你会说，我今天要在4点钟锻炼。

sentences.en: And then one of them gets sick, or another has a friend who comes over, and you can't leave or leave them.
sentences.zh: 然后其中一个生病了，或者另一个有朋友来家里玩，你无法离开他们。

sentences.en: Something always comes up.
sentences.zh: 总会有各种事情冒出来。

sentences.en: And then with your job, on top of it, it was just, it was impossible.
sentences.zh: 再加上你的工作，简直是……简直不可能。

sentences.en: Every night, I'd go back, and I'd go to bed, and I'd be like, okay, another failure.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上，我上床睡觉时都会想：好吧，又是一个失败的夜晚。

sentences.en: Until I decided that I was going to have to find a time when I could do it regularly, consistently.
sentences.zh: 直到我决定必须找一个可以定期、持续锻炼的时间。

sentences.en: And that was early in the morning.
sentences.zh: 那就是清晨。

sentences.en: So, I started running.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始跑步。

sentences.en: I was a committed runner for many years.
sentences.zh: 我做了多年的坚定跑步者。

sentences.en: I started running at 6 in the morning, and that was very hard to start off with, because for me, that didn't come naturally, and I really dreaded that.
sentences.zh: 我早上6点开始跑步，刚开始时非常艰难，因为对我来说这并不是天生就会的，我真的很害怕这一点。

sentences.en: But it got easier each time, and I actually did listen to the radio, and I found that to be a great sort of way to wake up, ultimately.
sentences.zh: 但每次都变得容易一些，而且我确实听了收音机，最终发现这是一种很棒的唤醒自己的方式。

sentences.en: One of the things I did to help was, I'm telling you all of my secrets here, I actually slept in my running clothes.
sentences.zh: 我为了坚持做的一件事是——我把所有的秘密都告诉你了——我其实是穿着跑步服睡觉的。

sentences.en: Um, because it made it easier to then get up and just get out the door early in the morning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为这让一大早起床并出门变得更容易了。

sentences.en: And then if I got back by 7 o'clock,
sentences.zh: 如果我能在7点前赶回来，

sentences.en: then I could make my boys breakfast and see them off to school and go live the rest of my day without having this worry about how I was going to get exercise in,
sentences.zh: 我就可以给我的男孩们做早餐，送他们去上学，然后去过我余下的生活，而不必担心在现有的日程安排下该如何抽时间锻炼。

sentences.en: given the rest of my schedule.
sentences.zh: 考虑到我其余的日程。

sentences.en: So, it worked.
sentences.zh: 所以，这行之有效。

sentences.en: So, what I find so interesting about that is that our conscious minds in some ways can help, but they help primarily not so much in terms of exercising willpower,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得最有趣的是，我们的意识在某种程度上确实能提供帮助，但它们发挥作用主要不是靠施展意志力，

sentences.en: but in scheming our ways to make the habit as frictionless as possible.
sentences.zh: 而是通过处心积虑地让习惯的阻力尽可能降到最低。

sentences.en: And so, in some ways, your conscious mind came up with this idea to say, let me sleep in my jogging clothes so when the alarm goes off at 6 o'clock,
sentences.zh: 因此，从某种意义上说，你的大脑想出了这个主意：让我穿着慢跑服睡觉，这样当6点的闹钟响起时，

sentences.en: I don't have the thought in my head, oh, no, I have to spend time changing before I go out.
sentences.zh: 我的脑海里就不会冒出“哦，不，出门前我还得花时间换衣服”这种想法。

sentences.en: You've just made it a little more frictionless, a little more easy.
sentences.zh: 你只是让它少了一点阻力，更容易实现了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: It's sort of like what professional chefs do.
sentences.zh: 这有点像专业厨师的做法。

sentences.en: So, I went up to the Culinary Institute of America and took a few of their preliminary classes, how they train chefs in something called mise en place,
sentences.zh: 我曾去美国烹饪学院参加过他们的一些初级课程，了解他们如何用一种叫“备料”（mise en place）的方法来培训厨师，

sentences.en: which is how to set up your environment to make it easy to create great dishes, consistently great dishes each time.
sentences.zh: 也就是如何布置好你的环境，以便每次都能轻松地烹制出美味、品质稳定的菜肴。

sentences.en: And they described to me the dilemma of beginning chefs, is they wanted to just jump in and do it, you know, let's just do it.
sentences.zh: 他们向我描述了初学厨师的困境，他们总是想直接上手就干，你知道的，“我们开始做吧”。

sentences.en: And they would get some flour, some sugar, some of the components together, and they'd try to start creating stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们会拿来一些面粉、糖和一些配料，然后就尝试开始制作。

sentences.en: But then they'd figure out, oh, no, I really need more flour, and I wasn't supposed to put all the sugar in here, and I was supposed to do something else there.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们会发现，“哦，不，我其实需要更多的面粉，我不该把所有的糖都加进这里，我本该在别的地方做点别的。”

sentences.en: And so, they have to learn, this is when they learn mise en place, putting everything in place before they actually begin.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们必须学习——这就是他们学习“备料”的时候——在真正开始之前把一切都就位。

sentences.en: And they put it in place in order.
sentences.zh: 而且他们是按顺序将一切摆放到位的。

sentences.en: So, they're not thinking a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们其实没怎么动脑筋。

sentences.en: They're not making decisions while they're actually cooking.
sentences.zh: 他们在真正做饭的时候并不需要做决定。

sentences.en: Instead, they are cued by all of the implements and the food and the prepared items in front of them on what goes next,
sentences.zh: 相反，摆在他们面前的所有用具、食材和备好的物品，会给他们提供下一步该做什么的暗示，

sentences.en: and it makes it much easier for them to be consistent and actually produce the same thing.
sentences.zh: 这让他们更容易保持连贯性，并真正做出相同品质的食物。

sentences.en: And I was impressed with that as a metaphor for behavior change, because if you structure the environment ahead of time, yes, it's work.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这可以作为一个很好的行为改变的比喻，因为如果你提前规划好环境，是的，这确实需要工作。

sentences.en: Yes, it does take executive control, our conscious thinking selves.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实需要动用执行控制力，也就是我们进行有意识思考的大脑。

sentences.en: But then we make it so much easier for us to sort of automate all of the other decisions so that in their case,
sentences.zh: 但随后，我们就能极其轻松地将所有其他决定自动化，这样对他们来说，

sentences.en: they can think about ways to make their current cakes even more wonderful and pastries even tastier as they put them together.
sentences.zh: 他们可以在组装糕点的同时，思考如何让现有的蛋糕更加美味，点心更加可口。

sentences.en: They can put the flourish into them because they have automated the basic components.
sentences.zh: 由于他们已经将基础环节自动化，他们就能在其中加入更多精妙的创意。

sentences.en: Wendy says you can also use friction in the opposite direction, to disrupt a habit.
sentences.zh: 温迪表示，你也可以反向利用阻力来打破习惯。

sentences.en: Think about campaigns to limit smoking.
sentences.zh: 想想限制吸烟的运动。

sentences.en: By the time the Surgeon General's report came out on the dangers of smoking, people had a pretty good idea.
sentences.zh: 等到美国卫生总监关于吸烟危害的报告发布时，人们其实已经有了相当深刻的认识。

sentences.en: It convinced people that they needed to stop smoking.
sentences.zh: 这说服了人们，让他们意识到自己需要戒烟。

sentences.en: But in fact, sales of cigarettes in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，美国的香烟销量

sentences.en: continued to increase into the 70s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代仍在继续增长。

sentences.en: So people were convinced, they knew it was not good for them, but they kept doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以人们虽然被说服了，也知道吸烟对身体不好，但他们还是在继续抽。

sentences.en: It was only once we started modifying the environment.
sentences.zh: 直到我们开始改造环境，情况才有所改变。

sentences.en: So warning labels on cigarette packs.
sentences.zh: 比如在烟盒上印上警告标签。

sentences.en: We removed vending machines.
sentences.zh: 我们撤掉了自动售货机。

sentences.en: I don't know if you remember cigarette vending machines, but you can't find them anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否还记得香烟自动售货机，但你现在已经找不到了。

sentences.en: Because there are now rules about how you can purchase cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 因为现在有了关于如何购买香烟的规定。

sentences.en: Cigarettes are typically put behind the counter, and you have to ask for them in order to purchase them.
sentences.zh: 香烟通常都被放在柜台后面，你必须开口询问才能买到。

sentences.en: We set bans on smoking in public places so that you can't easily anymore just light up in your office, in a restaurant, on a plane.
sentences.zh: 我们在公共场所颁布了禁烟令，这样你就不能再轻而易举地在办公室、餐厅或飞机上直接点烟了。

sentences.en: And then we started taxing.
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始征税。

sentences.en: We started taxing cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 我们开始对香烟征税。

sentences.en: All of that took huge political decision-making and commitment to make it happen.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都需要巨大的政治决策力和坚定决心才能实现。

sentences.en: But isn't it fascinating, Wendy, that telling people that smoking is going to give them, you know, emphysema and lung cancer,
sentences.zh: 但你不觉得很奇妙吗，温迪？告诉人们吸烟会导致，你知道的，肺气肿和肺癌，

sentences.en: that these things in some ways are less effective than telling them they have to walk 100 yards, get up from their desk, walk outside the building, and light up outside.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这些说辞的效用竟然还不如告诉他们必须步行100码、从办公桌前站起来、走到大楼外去抽烟。

sentences.en: You would think that the first would actually have much more effect than the second, but that does not turn out to be the case.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得前者的影响应该比后者大得多，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: We're pitiful.
sentences.zh: 我们真是太可悲了。

sentences.en: We would like to think that we are rational and respond to the data on cancer and emphysema,
sentences.zh: 我们总想觉得自己是理性的，能够对癌症和肺气肿的数据做出反应，

sentences.en: but the reality is we tend to act on autopilot on what we are doing already because it's so much easier.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，我们往往会出于惯性，对已经在做的事情开启自动驾驶模式，因为那样轻松太多了。

sentences.en: It's very hard to exert that kind of control.
sentences.zh: 要施加那种控制力是非常困难的。

sentences.en: So in a way, what the government was doing is it was making it easier for us to do the thing that we already wanted to do, which is to smoke less.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，政府所做的事情，其实是帮我们更轻松地去做我们本来就想做的事，那就是少抽烟。

sentences.en: We've talked about how you can decrease friction to build good habits and increase friction to dismantle bad habits.
sentences.zh: 我们之前讨论过如何通过减少阻力来养成好习惯，以及通过增加阻力来戒除坏习惯。

sentences.en: We've looked at how you can make healthy behaviors automatic and mindless and make unhealthy behaviors conscious and effortful.
sentences.zh: 我们探讨了如何让健康的行为变得自动化、无需费神，而让不健康的行为变得有意识、费力气。

sentences.en: Here are three additional ideas that build on these insights.
sentences.zh: 这里有三个建立在这些洞见之上的额外方法。

sentences.en: The first is something that Wendy calls piggybacking or stacking.
sentences.zh: 第一种是温迪称之为“顺便搭车”或“行为叠加”的方法。

sentences.en: It is taking a behavior that you're already doing and inserting a new behavior that you want to add.
sentences.zh: 也就是把你已经在做的一个行为，和你想加入的一个新行为结合起来。

sentences.en: So you want to remember to take your meds.
sentences.zh: 比如你想记住吃药。

sentences.en: Maybe you have meds prescribed by your doctor that you're supposed to take every night.
sentences.zh: 也许你医生给你开了一些药，要求你每晚服用。

sentences.en: If you want to remember to take them, a good way to do it is to put it on your nightstand,
sentences.zh: 如果你想记住吃药，一个好方法是把它放在你的床头柜上，

sentences.en: and then whatever you do last before you get into bed, is it turn off your phone, set your alarm, whatever it is,
sentences.zh: 然后把你上床睡觉前做的最后一件事——不管是关手机、定闹钟，还是别的什么——

sentences.en: just insert taking that pill in that stream of behavior, and over time, it will become automated,
sentences.zh: 把吃药这个动作直接插进那一连串的行为中，随着时间的推移，它就会变成自动化的，

sentences.en: much like the automated pattern that you're already performing.
sentences.zh: 就像你已经在执行的那些自动化模式一样。

sentences.en: In other words, you can essentially string habits together like a chain.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你基本上可以像串联链条一样把习惯串起来。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah, it's a sort of a shortcut to forming a new habit.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，这有点像是养成新习惯的捷径。

sentences.en: Use one that you already have.
sentences.zh: 利用你已经有的习惯。

sentences.en: Another powerful insight has to do with the role of what Wendy calls cues,
sentences.zh: 另一个深刻的见解与温迪所谓的“提示”的作用有关，

sentences.en: things that prompt you to do something.
sentences.zh: 也就是促使你去做某事的诱因。

sentences.en: Wendy mentioned cues in the context of the popcorn study.
sentences.zh: 温迪在爆米花研究的语境下提到过提示。

sentences.en: If you've ever been a smoker, you might have noticed there are certain triggers to your smoking.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经是个烟民，你可能会注意到某些特定的触发因素会让你想抽烟。

sentences.en: Maybe you come home at the end of the day, and you light up on your front porch.
sentences.zh: 也许你一天结束回家后，会在前廊点上一支烟。

sentences.en: The porch is what Wendy calls a cue.
sentences.zh: 这个前廊就是温迪所说的提示。

sentences.en: Cues are very powerful in creating new habits or preserving old ones.
sentences.zh: 提示在建立新习惯或保持旧习惯方面具有非常强大的力量。

sentences.en: Wendy uses cues in her own life to build new habits.
sentences.zh: 温迪在自己的生活中也利用提示来培养新习惯。

sentences.en: One cue for her is to wake up and have breakfast with her husband.
sentences.zh: 对她来说的一个提示就是醒来后和丈夫一起吃早餐。

sentences.en: That's her signal, her cue, that the next thing she needs to do is sit down at her computer and write for two hours.
sentences.zh: 那是她的信号、她的提示，告诉她接下来要做的事就是在电脑前坐下来写作两个小时。

sentences.en: If I give myself a couple of hours in the morning to write, if I structure it into my schedule,
sentences.zh: 如果我在早晨给自己留出几个小时来写作，如果我把它写进我的日程表里，

sentences.en: then I take away all of the decision-making and the stress about when and where I'm going to do it.
sentences.zh: 那么我就省去了关于何时何地去写作的所有决策和压力。

sentences.en: I don't mean to say that it makes writing easy.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这会让写作变得容易。

sentences.en: Writing is always a challenge for everyone.
sentences.zh: 对每个人来说，写作始终都是一项挑战。

sentences.en: But it does make the process easier.
sentences.zh: 但它确实让整个过程变得更容易了。

sentences.en: So I'm not all the time struggling about whether I should be doing this or something else.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会一直纠结于我是该做这个还是做别的。

sentences.en: That's being decided.
sentences.zh: 这件事已经决定好了。

sentences.en: This is part of my job, and I just need to do it.
sentences.zh: 这是我工作的一部分，我只需要去做就行了。

sentences.en: There's one last source of new habits, and it comes from an unexpected place.
sentences.zh: 新习惯的最后一个源头，来自于一个意想不到的地方。

sentences.en: Chaos.
sentences.zh: 混乱。

sentences.en: When our lives go haywire, the cues that normally surround us disappear.
sentences.zh: 当我们的生活陷入混乱时，平时包围着我们的提示就会消失。

sentences.en: Wendy says this can be a profound opportunity for reinvention.
sentences.zh: 温迪说，这可能是重塑自我的绝佳契机。

sentences.en: There's actually been a lot of research on something called habit discontinuity.
sentences.zh: 事实上，关于所谓的“习惯中断”，已经有很多相关研究了。

sentences.en: It's a jargony term, but it is studies of people when they're undergoing change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个听起来很专业的术语，其实就是对处于变故中的人们进行的研究。

sentences.en: And what we've learned is that that's an opportunity for people to try out new things
sentences.zh: 我们了解到的是，这是一个让人尝试新事物的机会，

sentences.en: that they didn't have the chance to do at, say, an old job or an old place where they lived.
sentences.zh: 这些新事物是他们在旧工作或旧居住地时没有机会去尝试的。

sentences.en: There's many such life disruptions, right?
sentences.zh: 生活中有很多这样的变故，对吧？

sentences.en: Relationships end.
sentences.zh: 一段关系的结束。

sentences.en: You get a family.
sentences.zh: 组建家庭。

sentences.en: Life gets disrupted.
sentences.zh: 生活被打乱。

sentences.en: And the typical way we think about that is that that's stressful and that that's not a good time for making new decisions.
sentences.zh: 我们对此的典型看法是，这充满压力，而且不是做出新决定的好时机。

sentences.en: But in fact, it actually turns out to be an opportunity for them to act more authentically on their values.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这最终被证明是一个让他们能够更真实地遵循内心价值观行事的契机。

sentences.en: So because they're making those decisions, they have to think, do I want to do this?
sentences.zh: 正因为他们在做出这些决定，他们必须思考：我想这么做吗？

sentences.en: How do I do this?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么做？

sentences.en: What are my new choices here?
sentences.zh: 我在这里的新选择是什么？

sentences.en: It's an opportunity to rethink some of the practical decisions you've made in your life
sentences.zh: 这是一个重新思考你在生活中做出的一些实用决策的机会，

sentences.en: and maybe to act more in ways that are consistent with how you want to be.
sentences.zh: 也许能让你更符合自己理想中的状态去行事。

sentences.en: Wendy Wood is a professor of psychology and business at the University of Southern California.
sentences.zh: 温迪·伍德是南加州大学心理学和商学教授。

sentences.en: She's the author of Good Habits, Bad Habits, The Science of Making Positive Changes That Stick.
sentences.zh: 她著有《好习惯，坏习惯：如何培养能坚持的积极改变》一书。

sentences.zh: 和你交谈非常愉快。
